definition: A subdivision of a main energy level, labelled s, p, d or f; within one level their energies increase in that order, and they contain 1, 3, 5 and 7 orbitals.
A region around the nucleus where an electron is most likely to be found; each orbital holds at most two electrons, with opposite spins.
The rule that electrons occupy the lowest-energy orbitals available first, so the order up to $Z = 36$ is 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d, 4p.
The rule that electrons in a sublevel occupy separate orbitals singly, with parallel spins, before any orbital takes a second electron.
The rule that one orbital holds at most two electrons, and two electrons sharing an orbital must have opposite spins.

How an atom's or ion's electrons are arranged in sublevels, written like 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ or in condensed form with a noble-gas core such as [Ar] 4s² 3d⁶; chromium and copper are the exceptions to the filling order up to $Z = 36$.
An electron in the outermost (highest) main energy level of an atom; for example, selenium has six, in 4s and 4p.
An electron alone in an orbital, with no partner of opposite spin; atoms or ions with unpaired electrons are attracted into a magnetic field.
